questions.subtopic: Domain 1: Cloud Concepts (Scalability vs Elasticity)
questions.question: Which scenario best illustrates the concept of 'horizontal scalability' in cloud computing architecture?
options: Adding more EC2 instances of equal size to an Auto Scaling group to distribute increased web traffic across a cluster
Upgrading a single virtual server from a t3.medium instance type to an m5.4xlarge instance type
Attaching a larger 2 TB EBS volume to an existing database server
Increasing the maximum clock frequency of a physical CPU hyper-thread
questions.explanation: Horizontal scaling (scaling out) involves adding more compute instances to distribute the workload across a cluster (e.g., using an Auto Scaling group with an Application Load Balancer). Vertical scaling (scaling up) involves adding more CPU or RAM to an existing single instance.
questions.citation: AWS Architecture Center — Horizontal vs Vertical Scaling
